issues.legal_issue: A conviction is unsafe when it rests on an uncorroborated oral dying declaration affected by material infirmities.
material_facts: The conviction rested entirely on an alleged oral dying declaration after the courts rejected the eyewitness evidence.
The two witnesses who claimed to hear the declaration did not disclose it for three days and offered no explanation for the delay.
A witness present at the scene did not report hearing the declaration, and one of the alleged hearers did not disclose the deceased’s alleged identification of the accused to him.
The witnesses said the deceased was not speaking clearly, was vomiting, and could not control his tongue; the medical evidence also raised doubt about his ability to make the statement.
There was no meaningful corroboration of the alleged declaration.
issues.conclusion: The Court held it highly unsafe to base the conviction on the oral dying declaration, gave the appellants the benefit of doubt, and set aside their convictions and sentences.
issues.legal_principle: An oral dying declaration is an important piece of evidence, but it should be free from infirmities. Where material infirmities, lack of corroboration, and doubt about the declarant’s ability to speak make reliance unsafe, the accused are entitled to the benefit of doubt. The judgment relied on no identified statutory provision or earlier case.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and conviction_based_entirely_on_oral_dying_declaration and delayed_disclosure_without_explanation and (witness_conduct_unreliable or medical_doubt_about_ability_to_speak) and no_meaningful_corroboration

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.conviction_based_entirely_on_oral_dying_: The conviction rests entirely on witnesses’ accounts of an oral statement made by a person who later died.
predicates.delayed_disclosure_without_explanation: The witnesses do not disclose the alleged statement for a substantial time and give no explanation for the delay.
predicates.witness_conduct_unreliable: The witnesses’ conduct or the surrounding evidence materially undermines the reliability of their account of the statement.
predicates.medical_doubt_about_ability_to_speak: Medical evidence or the described condition of the declarant raises doubt about the declarant’s ability to make the alleged statement.
predicates.no_meaningful_corroboration: No meaningful evidence independently supports the alleged statement.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction rests entirely on an oral dying declaration that was disclosed only after unexplained delay, is undermined by unreliable witness conduct or doubt about the declarant’s ability to speak, and lacks meaningful corroboration, the conviction is set aside on benefit of doubt.
